title: The tree's only ruleset reader never reads main-protect (deletion, non-fast-forward) or the release-tag ruleset
claim: tools/policy/counts.mjs:liveRequiredContexts fetches only rulesets that contribute a required_status_checks rule, so 1 of the repository's 3 active rulesets is compared with its record: dropping main-protect 22628467's deletion and non_fast_forward rules, adding an always-bypass actor to it, disabling it, or emptying release-tags-protect 23937752 each leaves requiredContextsDrift at 0 errors, while the same class of edit on 23698884 yields 1-7.
mechanism: The reader builds `ids` from branch rules filtered to type required_status_checks (counts.mjs, the `if (r.type !== 'required_status_checks') continue` line precedes `ids.add`), and requiredContextsDrift compares only the fetched objects; tools/ci/ruleset_cutover.py pins RULESET_ID = 23698884 alone. No other tracked script reads 22628467 or 23937752. The fixture's _comment records the choice: 22628467 is described there ('carries deletion and non-fast-forward') but deliberately left out of `rulesets`, so its rules are stated and never compared. Live re-read 2026-11-16 20:3x: 22628467's rules equal the capture.

evidence.unit: rulesets read (of 3 on the repository); gap_arms_unmoved=4 of 4, controls_fired=3 of 3
evidence.contention_note: fan-out, other seats running; counts are contention-immune

perturbation.change: counts.mjs:liveRequiredContexts: move `if (r.ruleset_id != null) ids.add(r.ruleset_id)` above the required_status_checks filter (harness --perturb)

metric_definition: Count of distinct ruleset ids liveRequiredContexts fetches from the captured API reads, and per arm the count of requiredContextsDrift error findings.
phenomenon_property: Every active ruleset targeting main or release tags is read and compared field by field with a committed record, so a change to any of them turns a check red.
seam_rule: gh api repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/rulesets --jq '.[].id' (each id not in the `read` list dev/audit/rounds/round11/D11/s3/ruleset_arms.py prints for the null arm)

null_control.value: null arm 0 errors; control arms on 23698884: 7, 1, 4
null_control.note: the controls show the comparator alive on the ruleset it reads, so the unmoved gap arms are the reader's scope, not a dead comparator

reproduction_steps: run the harness: null_errors=0, controls 7/1/4, every gap_* arm 0
run with --perturb: rulesets_read 2 and the 22628467 bypass arm fires
proposed_fix_scope: tools/policy/counts.mjs liveRequiredContexts also reads every other ruleset GET rulesets lists (main-protect 22628467, release-tags-protect 23937752) and compares each with a committed object in tools/policy/fixtures/required-contexts.json under a key of its own, beside ruleset_objects; the `rulesets` list keeps its #1300 meaning (the ids the required contexts are read out of), which the fixture's own _comment says must not name 22628467. bypass_actors stays token-hidden in CI as today. Mechanisation (D11.M5): extends an existing mechanical reader; cost about two API GETs per policy-docs run and about 20 lines, no policy line.
